steps.say: Sticky first stool can be the opening chapter of a lifelong salt transport disease. Thick protein rich gut contents glue the lower bowel shut before birth in a tenth of affected babies.
steps.tx: Sticky first stool can be the first clue to a lifelong disease. **Meconium ileus** (blocked first stool) is the earliest **cystic fibrosis** (salt transport disease) manifestation in **10 to 15 percent** (ten to fifteen percent) of patients, from **CFTR** (chloride channel gene) chloride failure making **80 to 90 percent** (eighty to ninety percent) protein secretions, with disease in **1 in 1000 to 2000 births** (one in one thousand to two thousand births). Thick gut contents glue the ileum shut before birth.

vis.alt: Diagram of CFTR gene effects on lungs, pancreas and intestines including meconium ileus.
vis.caption: One faulty chloride channel thickens lung mucus, starves digestion and glues the newborn gut into meconium ileus. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Three findings in the first two days define the simple case: a swollen belly, green vomiting and no first stool. The X ray shows frothy loops with no layering levels.
steps.tx: Three findings in two days define the simple case. The triad in the first **24 to 48 hours** (twenty four to forty eight hours) is generalized **abdominal distention** (swollen belly), **bilious emesis** (green vomiting) and no meconium, with polyhydramnios in **20 percent** (twenty percent). Films show a **soap bubble sign** (frothy ground glass loops) without air fluid levels, since thick meconium mixes with air instead of layering.

steps.say: The dye enema both diagnoses and often cures by pulling water into the sticky mass. Watch hydration closely throughout, because the burst risk, though small, is real.
steps.tx: The dye test treats as well as diagnoses. Water soluble **Gastrografin enema** (dye washout) shows a **microcolon** (tiny unused colon) with terminal pellets and relieves obstruction in **75 percent** (seventy five percent) by drawing water into the sticky mass, with **perforation** (burst gut) under **3 percent** (three percent) under close hydration watch. Keep fluids running and the baby warm throughout the washout.

steps.say: Once the blockage clears, prove the underlying disease before discharge. Salty sweat above the threshold confirms it, and gene testing gives a faster answer.
steps.tx: Prove the underlying disease after the blockage clears. **Pilocarpine iontophoresis** (sweat stimulation test) with chloride above **60 mEq per L** (sixty milliequivalents per litre) on a **sweat chloride test** (salty sweat measure) definitively confirms cystic fibrosis, with **CFTR gene** (disease gene) testing as the faster alternative. Every meconium ileus baby earns one of these two tests before discharge.

vis.alt: Diagram of the CFTR chloride defect in airways and sweat glands with multisystem effects including newborn meconium ileus.
vis.caption: CFTR failure leaves sweat salty above 60 and glues the newborn gut into meconium ileus. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: When washouts fail, surgeons open the bowel and flush rather than cut length away. A mucus thinning wash that snaps mucus links usually clears the plug.
steps.tx: When washouts fail, open and flush rather than cut away. Failed enema or **5 mL** (five millilitres) of **10 percent** (ten percent) **N-acetylcysteine** (mucus thinner) every **6 hours** (six hours) by tube leads to surgery, where **enterotomy** (bowel opening) with warm saline or **4 percent** (four percent) acetylcysteine washout that breaks **disulfide bonds** (mucus links) plus mucosal sparing evacuation beats routine resection. Save every centimetre of ileum.

steps.say: A leak before birth leaves chalky fossils on the film and walled off spill. Older children get a different blockage from missed enzymes or dryness, which usually melts with washouts.
steps.tx: A burst before birth leaves fossils on film. Complicated disease with in utero perforation gives **calcification** (chalky specks), **meconium pseudocyst** (walled off spill), adhesive peritonitis or ascites on film, while **DIOS** (distal ileal blockage) in older patients from missed enzymes or dehydration usually responds to enemas or oral polyethylene glycol. Calcification means the leak happened long ago.

steps.say: Lifelong enzyme capsules fix digestion but can scar the colon in heavy doses. Bloody stools or narrowing in a supplemented child should trigger dose review and colon imaging.
steps.tx: Lifelong enzymes carry their own bowel risk. High strength pancreatic **enzyme replacement** (enzyme capsules) treats **exocrine insufficiency** (poor digestion) but can cause **fibrosing colonopathy** (scarred colon), needing stricture resection. Bloody stools or narrowing in a heavily supplemented child should prompt dose review and colon imaging before the scarring tightens.

steps.say: A different plug disease usually spares the knife and points at missing bowel nerves instead. The same dye enema both proves and removes it, with no operation needed.
steps.tx: A different plug disease spares the knife. **Meconium plug syndrome** (colon plug blockage) is usually not cystic fibrosis but signals **Hirschsprung disease** (missing nerve bowel), maternal diabetes or hypothyroidism. Films show a **microcolon** (tiny colon) packed with plugs up to the dilated proximal colon, and contrast enema both diagnoses and cures without surgery. Always rule out Hirschsprung after.
